source.paraphrase: The solver guarantee is uniform for initial distance at most a prescribed radius. The reduction repeatedly requests accuracy alpha times the squared scheduled radius divided by8, halves that radius, and finally calls the solver at requested accuracy. The source describes per-stage cost phi(8*kappa), final cost phi(kappa), and an O(phi(8*kappa) log(alpha R²/epsilon)) total. It first writes actual initial distances, then substitutes upper radius schedules. Positive moduli and tolerances, admissible logarithm domains, and a cost-comparison convention are not all stated. Lemma4.2 is a separate reverse reduction by quadratic regularization.

load_bearing_reuse.use: Apply at minimizing z and arbitrary y, derive gradient(z)=0 via hmin.isLocalMin Filter.univ_mem and fderiv_eq_zero (as existing GradientDescentContraction). Obtain alpha/2*norm(y-z)^2<=f(y)-f(z). Genuine strong convexity plus true derivatives, no supplied QG assumption.

load_bearing_reuse.warning: This existing differentiability-free midpoint lemma has alpha/4, explicitly not sharp alpha/2. At tolerance alpha Rk²/8 it only proves radius Rk/sqrt2, so cannot be used for the intended halving constant.

load_bearing_reuse.use: Concrete non-oracle-dependent test consumer: run actual convex GD with a supplied radius-based natural budget to realize a convex solver. Avoid tests consisting only of A returning z, since that tests analysis but not a useful solver.

recommended_contract.space: Complete real Hilbert E, actual differentiable or C1 f, StrongConvexOn univ alpha f, alpha>0, supplied global minimizer z. Beta>0 is the solver class parameter. If all smoothness/convex solver correctness is supplied as an abstract solver contract, explicitly scope theorem as reduction adapter for that contract, not a newly verified first-order oracle machine.
recommended_contract.solver: Prefer A(x,r,delta) and cost(x,r,delta), or a single returned point/cost pair, with a contract for every delta>0 and r>0, norm(x-z)<=r: returned gap<=delta and cost<=phi(beta*r²/delta). The numerical radius is a supplied upper bound and need not equal an unknown actual distance. A may be specialized to f; it must not take the unknown z as an algorithm input.
recommended_contract.recursion: Rk=R/(2^k), x0 supplied, x(k+1)=A(xk,Rk,alpha Rk²/8). Define this actual recursion once using Nat.rec or a transparent recursive def. Prove norm(xk-z)<=Rk by induction, and the actual kth call gap and cost bounds.
recommended_contract.final_call: For K with alpha*(R/(2^K))²<=epsilon, invoke A(xK,sqrt(epsilon/alpha),epsilon), whose radius budget is justified and whose cost argument equals kappa. Alternatively use scheduled RK for final call and either retain phi(beta RK²/epsilon) or assume appropriate monotonicity.
recommended_contract.finite_total: Define total as sum k in range K of actual per-call costs plus actual final-call cost. Conclude finite total<=K*phi(8*kappa)+phi(kappa). Natural-valued costs avoid negative-query artifacts; phi may be natural-valued or nonnegative real-valued with casts stated.
recommended_contract.substantive_delta: Actual radius-invariant recursion plus composed finite cost and final objective accuracy is the new integration edge. A one-step QG wrapper, or a theorem assuming all stage radius invariants/cost bounds and merely restating them, is not sufficient.
recommended_contract.optional_exact_round_count: For R>0,epsilon>0 choose K=Nat.ceil(log(alpha R²/epsilon)/log4), using log4>0 and Nat.le_ceil. No additional max0 needed for natural ceiling. A simpler initial theorem may accept the algebraic final-radius condition and leave the logarithmic consumer explicitly uncovered if proof size grows.

hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.issue: Upper radius versus actual radius; phi monotonicity
hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.analysis: The source definition gives a uniform upper-radius solver guarantee. If the formal contract preserves this, scheduled stage argument beta Rk²/(alpha Rk²/8)=8kappa is exact and needs no monotonicity. If the only premise instead bounds cost by phi(beta*actualDistance²/delta), substituting Rk requires monotonic phi on the relevant interval. Do not silently treat actual distance as the known radius.

Even under the uniform radius contract, replacing Kphi(8kappa)+phi(kappa) by (K+1)phi(8kappa) requires at least phi(kappa)<=phi(8kappa). Monotonic phi suffices but is stronger than needed; without it keep the additive exact cost. This is a source convention/omission to expose and separately audit.

hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.issue: Bare logarithmic big-O at large tolerance
hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.analysis: For q=alpha R²/epsilon<=1 the logarithm is nonpositive, while the final polishing call can still have positive cost. Even q approaching1 from above cannot uniformly absorb that call into C logq. A global bound needs 1+max(0,logq), or a quantitatively small-tolerance regime q>=c>1. Do not silently interpret the printed big-O expression as globally valid.

hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.issue: Zero rounds do not imply objective accuracy
hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.analysis: R²<=epsilon/alpha is distance information. With beta much greater than alpha, initial objective error can exceed epsilon. Keep the actual final solver call even when K0; do not simply return x0 based on this radius criterion.

R0 implies x0=z and already zero gap; return x0 with zero additional calls. The proposed alpha Rk²/8 calls have zero tolerance at R0 and violate a positive-tolerance solver contract, so separate R0 or state R>0 for recursion theorem.

hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.issue: Abstract cost is not verified oracle trace
hidden_domains_and_failure_boundaries.analysis: An output/cost function under a supplied contract proves a conditional solver reduction and cost composition. It does not by itself prove the returned cost equals a first-order query count or that the solver cannot access z. A class-level existential algorithm reduction needs explicit oracle-realizability discipline or must remain outside this adapter scope.
Lemma4.2 needs separate minimizer, curvature/smoothness and approximation-transfer adapters; do not claim both-direction equivalence from Lemma4.1 restart alone.

focused_tests: Actual nontrivial quadratic plus a radius/tolerance-based convex GD solver; exercise more than one restart, actual changing point and finite accumulated cost.
A deliberately loose supplied radius checks that solver contract uses an upper bound rather than secretly requiring exact initial norm.
K0 with alpha small relative to beta: demonstrate the final polishing call is retained.
Zero-radius branch avoids all positive-tolerance calls; log consumer includes q<=1 and ordinary positive-domain q>1.
If no monotonicity is imposed, use nonmonotone phi with phi(kappa)>phi(8kappa) to demonstrate why additive final cost cannot be silently absorbed.
